June 1, 1937.    Afternoon Translation.

Yih Chin (益群), a semi-monthly, Issue No. 29 :-

THE G.P.U.--THE SOVIET'S DREADED SECRET ORGANIZATION

The G.P.U. is a Soviet espionage organ formed after the Russian Revolution. It is under the direct control of the Soviet People's Committee. The organization of the G.P.U. is as follows:
(1) Military Department. Members of this department, numbering some 100,000, are scattered in the Red Army, frontier troops and all other military organizations both inside and outside the country. The greatest number are to be found among troops stationed in the Far East. Their duties are to keep observation on the reactionary elements in the Army and to make secret enquiries about the military activities and constructions of foreign countries on the frontier.
(2) Foreign Department. Members of this department are disguised as employees of Soviet diplomatic organs in foreign countries, merchants, travellers, homeless White Russians, etc. Their duties are to pry out diplomatic and military secrets of foreign countries, propagate Communism, direct class warfare, and keep a watch on Soviet officials, merchants and White Russians in foreign countries.
(3) Intelligence Department. The duty of this department is to collect various information and supply it to Government organs.
(4) Administrative Department. This department is in charge of all internal administrative affairs of the G.P.U.
(5) Printing Department. This department prints and supplies members of the G.P.U. with Communistic pamphlets and publications.

The G.P.U. has a total membership of between 160,000 and 200,000, and may be said to be a secret organization possessing the same powers as the Police, the Military Police and the Judicial organs.

The Intelligence Department is the most important department in the G.P.U. Apart from its own members, the members of the Communist Party in the Union also have it as their duty to report any anti-Communist organization that they may discover, and in foreign countries traitors are employed to act as spies. Thus the total number of persons working under directions of the G.P.U. directly or indirectly amount to more than a million.

Efforts are being made to increase the number of members of the G.P.U. Usually the persons whom the G.P.U. desires to become members are forced to do so on pain of losing their ordinary employment.

Inside the U.S.S.R., G.P.U. spies can be found in every class of people from Government officials down to labourers.

When any plot against the Soviet Government is discovered, the plotters are not immediately arrested. Instead, the G.P.U. details its members to get into the secret and help the plot to develop until all the persons taking part in it are known to the G.P.U. They are then arrested en bloc. 1937年6月1日。下午译件。

《益群》，半月刊，第29期：

格别乌——苏维埃令人畏惧的秘密组织

格别乌（G.P.U.）是俄国革命后成立的苏维埃间谍机构。它直接受苏维埃人民委员会控制。格别乌的组织结构如下：
(1) 军事部。该部门成员约10万人，散布于红军、边防部队以及国内外所有其他军事组织中。人数最多者见于驻扎在远东的部队。其职责是监视军队中的反动分子，并秘密调查外国在边境地区的军事活动和建设情况。
(2) 外交部。该部门成员伪装成苏联驻外外交机构雇员、商人、旅行者、无家可归的白俄人等。其职责是刺探外国的外交和军事机密，宣传共产主义，指导阶级斗争，并监视在国外的苏联官员、商人和白俄人。
(3) 情报部。该部门的职责是收集各种信息并提供给政府机构。
(4) 行政部。该部门负责格别乌的所有内部行政事务。
(5) 印刷部。该部门负责印刷并向格别乌成员提供共产主义小册子和出版物。

格别乌总人数在16万至20万之间，可以说是一个拥有与警察、宪兵和司法机关同等权力的秘密组织。

情报部是格别乌最重要的部门。除了其自身成员外，联盟内的共产党员也有义务报告他们发现的任何反共组织，而在国外则雇佣叛徒充当间谍。因此，直接或间接在格别乌指导下工作的人员总数超过一百万。

当局正努力增加格别乌的成员数量。通常，格别乌希望成为其成员的人会被强迫加入，否则将面临失去正常工作的风险。

在苏联境内，从政府官员到劳工，各个阶层中都能发现格别乌的间谍。

当发现针对苏维埃政府的阴谋时，策划者不会立即被捕。相反，格别乌会派遣其成员潜入秘密组织内部，帮助阴谋发展，直到所有参与人员都被格别乌知晓。然后他们会遭到集体逮捕。不久前，一个反斯大林组织

Attache to the Soviet Embassy in Great Britain, was recalled
to his country and executed for being concerned in the affair.
A number of G.P.U. members are charged with the
special duty of investigating the people's private property.
Persons found in possession of property in excess of the
legal limit will have their property confiscated; to some
extent their lives will also be in danger.
Spies attached to the Foreign Department of the
G.P.U. carry out extensive activities in the interior parts
of foreign countries. Foreign Communists are utilized,
while large quantities of money are spent to buy over
foreign traitors. Kureta, a Japanese clerk employed by
the Soviet Embassy in Japan, and Otake, Director of the
Russian Affairs Study Bureau of Japan, who were arrested
following the February 26 outbreak in Japan, belonged to the
latter category of persons. The Foreign Department spends
$60,000,000 annually, half of which is used to pay foreign
traitors.
There is a passport forging office in the
G.P.U. able to forge the passport of any country. Many
G.P.U. spies, armed with forged U.S.A. passports and
disguised as Americans, are in Japan and China carrying out
their missions. Many Soviet spies in foreign countries
belong to the General Staff of the Red Army, but their
espionage activities are confined to military secrets.
Insurgents against the Soviet Government, when
arrested by members of the G.P.U., are publicly sentenced to
death or secretly executed according to circumstances.
Sometimes assassination is resorted to.
When a person upon being arrested by the G.P.U.
refuses to make a statement, he is prevented from sleep by
having a strong light directed against his eyes. After two
or three days, the person becomes mentally deranged or even
mad. He then gives out information or discloses secrets
required by the G.P.U.
The G.P.U. is also very active in watching the
foreign spies in U.S.S.R. The search of the British
Embassy in U.S.S.R. and the detention of the Ambassador a
few years ago was one of the actions of the G.P.U.
Undoubtedly the G.P.U. will play an active part
in the next World War.

1937年6月1日。下午译件。
被发现，苏联驻英国大使馆武官“纳-德-拉”（柳德权）(?普特纳 Putna) 将军被召回国，并因牵涉此事而被处决。
部分格别乌成员负有调查民众私有财产的特殊职责。被发现持有超过法定限额财产的人，其财产将被没收；在某种程度上，他们的生命也会受到威胁。
隶属于格别乌外交部的间谍在外国内地开展广泛活动。他们利用外国共产党人，并花费大量金钱收买外国叛徒。日本驻苏联大使馆雇用的日本职员仓田（Kureta），以及在日本二二六事变后被捕的日本俄罗斯事务研究局局长大竹（Otake），就属于后一类人。外交部每年支出6,000万美元，其中一半用于支付外国叛徒。
格别乌内设有一个护照伪造办公室，能够伪造任何国家的护照。许多格别乌间谍手持伪造的美国护照，伪装成美国人，在日本和中国执行任务。许多在国外的苏联间谍隶属于红军总参谋部，但他们的间谍活动仅限于军事机密。
反对苏维埃政府的起义者被格别乌成员逮捕后，视情况被公开判处死刑或秘密处决。有时也会采取暗杀手段。
当某人被格别乌逮捕后拒绝供认时，他会通过强光照射眼睛的方式被剥夺睡眠。两三天后，此人会出现精神错乱甚至发疯。随后他会提供格别乌所需的信息或泄露机密。
格别乌在监视苏联境内的外国间谍方面也非常活跃。几年前搜查苏联境内的英国大使馆并拘留大使的行动，就是格别乌的行动之一。
毫无疑问，格别乌将在下一次世界大战中发挥积极作用。

The "Shanghai Zaria" of February 2,5 and 7 writes as follows:
Soviet.

Soviet military espionage in China.

At present, work by the Soviet Red Army Intelligence Office is being conducted in foreign countries as it was during the Tsarist regime. Always keeping in mind the main military principle that, for successful military operations, it is necessary to study in detail the military strength and technical preparedness of a potential enemy, the Bolsheviks attach great importance to the work of their War Intelligence Office.

The Bolshevik military intelligence [illegible] as far as the importance of the work is performed by it is [illegible] by the Bolsheviks to be equal to that of the [illegible] although it is kept in the background. Profiting from the lessons of the Great War, the Bolsheviks have organized their espionage system on a large scale. They have retained all that is useful from the old Csarist army and put it into operation, adjusting it to the new modern conditions of international espionage.

The Bolsheviks have not spent such a long time exclusively in the organization of their present system which began to function definitely at the beginning of 1927. It can be asserted with the greatest confidence that at present there is no country in which the Bolsheviks do not have their network of spies.

Of course, the soviet espionage work in foreign countries encounters great difficulties. Instead of [illegible] stated that USSR is spending very large sums of money on espionage activities work, it must be stated that this information is true only with regard to the Komintern and the [illegible]. These two organizations, it is true, swallow up the greatest part of the funds while the war intelligence work is poorly paid. The War Office officials are always complaining about this injustice and state that if even half of the amount spent by the Komintern were to be given to them they would produce more profitable work than the political spies and this latter should then be dissolved. The lack of money not infrequently spoils their work by not permitting them to carry out all their plans.

The intelligence agents receive instructions almost by every post to observe economy as much as possible. Thus the agents are often obliged to spend their own salary which they are refunded only two months later. The money question, however is a secondary one. The main difficulty lies in the fact that the soviet secret agents, who reside in foreign countries, are being carefully watched not only by the police and secret agents of the country in which they reside, but also by the all secret agents of other countries. Everyone is trying to detect the soviet secret agents, who always form an interesting subject for detection. Espionage work is a sort of sport. As in sport, the opponents try to outwit their enemy, so in a similar manner every agent does his best to outwit the enemy agent. The only difference is that in sport one has one's opponent before one; whereas in espionage work one has first to find out one's enemy.

While secret agents of every country are not easily to say two or three dozen, those of Russ. are unknown. Their identification in their connection with the soviet secret service, which is being [illegible] by all governments as an international menace, are difficult to detect as they work in strict secrecy, carefully avoiding any error which might lead to their detection. In spite of the difficulties which soviet agents encounter

2月2日、5日和7日的《上海扎里亚报》（Shanghai Zaria）写道：
苏维埃。

苏维埃在华军事间谍活动。

目前，苏联红军情报局在外国的活动方式与沙皇统治时期一样。布尔什维克始终牢记主要的军事原则，即为了成功的军事行动，必须详细研究潜在敌人的军事实力和技术准备状况，因此他们非常重视战争情报局的工作。

就工作的重要性而言，布尔什维克军事情报[原文不清]被认为与[原文不清]同等重要，尽管它保持在幕后。吸取大战的教训，布尔什维克大规模组织了他们的间谍系统。他们保留了旧沙皇军队中有用的部分并投入运作，使其适应国际间谍活动的现代新条件。

布尔什维克并非花了很长时间专门组织他们目前的系统，该系统于1927年初开始明确运作。可以最有把握地断言，目前没有一个国家没有布尔什维克的间谍网。

当然，苏维埃在外国的间谍工作面临巨大困难。与其说[原文不清]声称苏联在间谍活动工作上花费了巨额资金，不如说这一信息仅对共产国际和[原文不清]属实。确实，这两个组织吞没了大部分资金，而战争情报工作的报酬很低。战争局官员总是抱怨这种不公，并表示即使将共产国际花费的一半金额给他们，他们也能产生比政治间谍更有成效的工作成果，而后者的机构理应解散。资金的缺乏常常使他们无法执行所有计划，从而破坏了他们的工作。

情报人员几乎每收到一次邮件指示，都要尽可能节约开支。因此，特工们经常不得不垫付自己的薪水，而这些薪水要在两个月后才能报销。然而，资金问题是次要的。主要困难在于，居住在外国的苏维埃秘密特工不仅受到居住国警察和秘密特工的严密监视，还受到其他国家所有秘密特工的监视。每个人都试图侦测苏维埃秘密特工，因为他们始终是一个有趣的侦测对象。间谍工作是一种运动。就像在运动中对手试图智胜敌人一样，每个特工也尽力智胜敌方特工。唯一的区别是，在运动中对手就在面前；而在间谍工作中，必须先找出敌人。

虽然每个国家的秘密特工不难说出两三个 dozen（打），但俄罗斯的特工却无人知晓。由于各国政府都将苏维埃秘密服务视为国际威胁，要识别与该系统有关的特工十分困难，因为他们在严格保密的情况下工作，小心避免任何可能导致暴露的错误。尽管苏维埃特工面临种种困难

the Union of the Soviet Socialist Republics however not unfrequently
obtain good results from this work, owing to certain particular features
of the organisation and to the selection of the personal staff. The
staff of soviet spies in foreign countries is selected not from amongst
persons desiring engage in this work, but from those who in the opinion
of the soviets may be useful and necessary. This system is responsible
for the fact that soviet secret agents are very seldom recalled which
practice takes place among the other foreign official representatives
at Moscow.

The present article deals only with the espionage work of the
Soviet War Office Intelligence and chiefly of the staff of the Sibe-
rian Military District whose territory borders China.

There are operating simultaneously in Chinese territory two
distinct espionage organisations of the Red Army. The Intelligence
Office of the Red Army General Staff with its headquarters in Moscow, x
and the Siberian Army Corps Intelligence (Intelligence) Branch Office
with its headquarters at Novo-Sibirsk. For convenience sake we will
designate the first as headquarters No 3 and the second as Headquarters
No 7 which correspond to their respective official designations in the
general scheme of the organisation of the Red Army.

These organisations have divided the whole of China into two
sections - Southern and Northern and seat of the Southern section
for both organisations is at Shanghai, whereas the Northern seat of
No 3 headquarters is in Harbin while that of No 3 headquarters is at
Pogranichnaia Railway station..

For practical purposes and more effective management No 7 Headquar-
ters has established its Branch Intelligence Office at Vladivostock
which is managed by the Assistant Chief of No 7 Headquarters. In order
to observe secrecy he resides there in disguise. The official position
of the Assistant Chief of No 7 Headquarters at Vladivostock is that of
the Director of the scientific Institution "The Bureau for the Export
and Import of Beans" Several specialists work in this Bureau but the
majority of the staff are military officers attached to No 7 Headquar-
ters.

Sometimes the Chief of the No 7 Headquarters at Vladivostock offi-
cially represents other commercial organisations. This is made possible
through the monopoly of all the foreign and home trade which is in the
hands of Director of Gostorg. Gostorg is kept informed of the actual
activities of the Chief of No 7 Headquarters at Vladivostock and ren-
ders him every assistance. Such adoption of functions by the chief of
No 7 Headquarters as a commercial representative take place in the
negotiations of all soviet trading institutions with foreigners when
the presence of representative of the G.P.U. is imperative.

In addition to this Bureau, which is managed by the Chief of No 7
Headquarters, there exists in Vladivostock still another department
closely connected with it, whose chief is one of the assistants of the
Chief of No 7 Headquarters. It is called the "Bureau for foreign vessels
service". In this case the majority of the agents are likewise members
of No 7 Headquarters. These two institutions, so to speak. are mono-
polised by the staff of No 7 Headquarters for their particular work.

There are quite a number of other Soviet institutions in which
agents of No 7. Headquarters are employed on a secondary jobs and the
chiefs of said institutions never suspect them to be working for the
intelligence office. Among such institutions at Vladivostock are the
following: "The Commercial Agency of the Chinese Eastern Railway",
"The Egersheld Corn Stock Exchange" etc. All these institutions present
considerable interest to the War Intelligence Office owing to their
constant intercourse with foreigners.

By indirect pressure on the part of these Intelligence Branches,
the above institutions strive to foster and increase their relations
with foreign countries. Usually this is effected under the guise of
commercial operations and should the relations promise good results

然而，苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（Union of the Soviet Socialist Republics）却经常从这项工作中获得良好的结果，这归功于其组织的某些特定特征以及对人员的选择。驻外国的苏联间谍人员并非从那些希望从事此项工作的人中选拔，而是从那些被苏维埃认为有用且必要的人中选拔。这一制度导致苏联秘密特工很少被召回，而在莫斯科的其他外国官方代表中，召回做法却很常见。

本文仅涉及苏联陆军部情报局的间谍活动，主要是西伯利亚军区参谋部的人员，该军区的领土与中国接壤。

在中国领土上，同时运作着两个截然不同的红军间谍组织。一个是总部设在莫斯科的红军总参谋部情报局 x ，另一个是总部设在新西伯利亚（Novo-Sibirsk）的西伯利亚军团情报（分支）办事处。为方便起见，我们将前者称为第3号总部，后者称为第7号总部，这与它们在红军总体组织架构中的正式代号相对应。

这些组织将整个中国划分为两个区域——南部和北部。两个组织的南部区域中心均设在上海，而第3号总部的北部中心设在哈尔滨，第3号总部的[另一]北部中心则设在波格拉尼奇纳亚（Pogranichnaia）火车站。（注：原文此处重复提及“第3号总部”，疑似有误，但依要求照实翻译）

出于实际目的和更有效的管理，第7号总部在海参崴（Vladivostock）设立了其分支情报办事处，由第7号总部助理主任管理。为了保密，他伪装身份居住在那里。第7号总部助理主任在海参崴的公开身份是科学机构“豆类进出口局”的局长。该局有几名专家工作，但大多数工作人员是隶属于第7号总部的军官。

有时，第7号总部驻海参崴的主任在官方上代表其他商业组织。这是通过垄断所有对外贸易和国内贸易实现的，而这些贸易掌握在国家贸易总局（Gostorg）局长手中。国家贸易总局了解第7号总部驻海参崴主任的实际活动，并向他提供一切协助。当国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）代表的出席成为必要时，第7号总部主任以商业代表身份履行职能的做法，便出现在所有苏联贸易机构与外国人的谈判中。

除了这个由第7号总部主任管理的局之外，海参崴还存在另一个与其密切相关的部门，其负责人是第7号总部主任的助理之一。它被称为“外籍船舶服务局”。在这种情况下，大多数特工同样也是第7号总部的成员。可以说，这两个机构被第7号总部的人员垄断，用于其特定工作。

还有许多其他苏联机构，其中雇佣了第7号总部的特工从事次要工作，而这些机构的负责人从未怀疑他们是在为情报局工作。海参崴的此类机构包括：“中东铁路商业代理处”、“艾格斯赫尔德（Egersheld）谷物交易所”等。由于这些机构与外国人保持经常往来，它们引起了陆军情报局的极大兴趣。

通过这些情报分支机构的间接施压，上述机构努力培养并增加与外国的关系。通常这是在商业操作的幌子下进行的，如果这种关系有望为陆军部带来良好结果，

These institutions through their indirect participation in War Office
Intelligence work, allow this latter to place at their disposal a grea-
ter number of agents than they can afford to pay. Every agent of No 7
Headquarters who is commissioned to any of these institutions, receives
his renumeration from the latter, whereas No 7 Headquarters pay him
only a small allowance. This permits the War Office to economise on its
estimates and to use the surplus for the employment of more agents.
Intelligence agents, posted in the various institutions, receive lighter
jobs which do not demand too much of their time, which latter is emplo-
ying for intelligence work. In addition agents work overtime for which
they do not receive any salary.
In the War Office administration there exists an order to the effect
that should overtime work be practised this means that the employees
are incapable of carrying out their work and are liable to dismissal
from the army, but this order does not affect the secret service agents.
These latter work constantly without any limit of time. The informer of
the No 7 Headquarters do not come under this rule. They, like the agents
of the G.P.U. do not work in Headquarters offices. Their work consists
exclusively in tracing out secret agents of foreign countries, i.e.foreign
spies.

No 7 Headquarters has a large number of informers at its disposal,
whose task consists chiefly of reporting on foreign secret agents. For
instance at Vladivostock all "Laundries" and "Barber shops" and foreign
businesses of a similar nature have long since been "spotted" and their
activities turned to profit by NO 7 Headquarters. Should any of these
kind of business show signs of resistance, they are simply "liquida-
ted without further ado. For instance, it was discovered that a lady
teacher teaching a foreign language at the Vladivostock Infantry school,
worked for a certain foreign country. Further observation proved that
she worked alone i.e. without assistance of informers. The attempt to
win her by the G.P.U. proved unsuccessful therefore she was deported
from the Maritime province and forbidden to work in any of the military
institutions.
A similar case happened to the owner of a shop dealing in military
articles who was suspected of being spy. The business did not show any
profit to the owner although he paid very high taxes. At the suggestion
of No 7 Headquarters the Finance Inspector increased the taxes to an
amount which exceeds the gross receipt. The owner paid them without protesting,
which only served to heighten the suspicion against him. As there was
no other evidence against him, he was arrested after a careful search
of his premises and imprisoned for two months. Finally he was deported
from the Maritime Province.
Now we shall see how the espionage work of the No 7 Headquarters
is organised. The Vladivostock branch of No 7 Headquarters has its
secret agents in the following places on the territory of USSR: Posiet,
Poltavka, Grodekovo, Iman and Blagoveschensk. There are also soviet se-
cret agents of the No 7 Headquarters in Chinese territory. The liaison
between these agents over the frontier is maintained with the aid of
smugglers while the Railway serves the region of Grodekovo-Pogranichnaia.
Not one of the smugglers is aware that he is an espionage instru-
ment. The majority of the secret agents near the frontier are known as
smugglers. The region around Manchuli station and all adjacent points po-
ssess agents of the 18 and 19 Army Corps. This however does not prevent
the work of the agents of the No 3 Headquarters and No 3 Headquarters.
The only difference is that these agents in conducting their work have
no direct communication with USSR, but always report directly to Harbin.
In every Chinese provincial city there is a special resident conduc-
ting work that covers the whole province and he has his agents in all
the district towns. In cases where there are no district agent, the
provincial agent has 2 or 3 men who periodically travel and col-
lect information according to a previously planned program. All infor-
mation collected by the provincial residential agent both in the provin-
cial towns and also in the administrative institutions of the country
town are sent periodically, not less than weekly, to Harbin and Vladivos-
tock by special messenger. These messengers bring back with them new in-
structions, money and private letters from Russia.

那么商业利益便不予考虑。这些机构通过间接参与陆军部的情报工作，使得陆军部能够支配比其自身财力所能支付的更多的特工。每一位被派往这些机构的第7号总部特工，其薪酬由这些机构支付，而第7号总部只支付少量津贴。这使得陆军部能够节省预算，并将结余用于雇佣更多特工。派驻在各机构的情报特工承担较轻的工作任务，不占用太多时间，从而将时间用于情报工作。此外，特工们还进行无薪加班。

陆军部行政系统中有一项规定，大意是如果实行加班，则意味着员工无法胜任工作，并可能被军队解雇，但这项规定不影响秘密服务特工。后者持续工作，没有任何时间限制。第7号总部的线人也不受此规则约束。他们像国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的特工一样，不在总部办公室工作。他们的工作 exclusively 在于追踪外国的秘密特工，即外国间谍。

第7号总部拥有大量线人，其主要任务是报告外国秘密特工的情况。例如，在海参崴，所有的“洗衣店”和“理发店”以及类似性质的外国企业早已被“标记”，其活动被第7号总部利用以牟取情报利益。如果这类 businesses 表现出任何抵抗迹象，它们就会被干脆地“清理”掉，不再多言。例如，发现一名在海参崴步兵学校教授外语的女教师为某个外国工作。进一步的观察证明她是单独行动，即没有线人协助。国家政治保卫局试图收编她但未成功，因此她被驱逐出滨海省，并被禁止在任何军事机构工作。

类似的情况也发生在一家经营军用物品的商店店主身上，他被怀疑是间谍。尽管该店主缴纳很高的税款，但他的生意并未显示任何利润。在第7号总部的建议下，税务督察将税额提高到超过毛收入的金额。店主毫无抗议地支付了税款，这反而加深了对他的怀疑。由于没有其他针对他的证据，在对他的场所进行仔细搜查后，他被逮捕并监禁了两个月。最终，他被驱逐出滨海省。

现在我们将看看第7号总部的间谍工作是如何组织的。第7号总部海参崴分支在苏联领土上的以下地点拥有秘密特工：波谢特（Posiet）、波尔塔夫卡（Poltavka）、格罗杰科沃（Grodekovo）、伊曼（Iman）和布拉戈维申斯克（Blagoveschensk）。在中国领土上也有第7号总部的苏联秘密特工。这些跨境特工之间的联络依靠走私者维持，而铁路则服务于格罗杰科沃-波格拉尼奇纳亚地区。没有一个走私者意识到自己是间谍工具。边境附近的大多数秘密特工以走私者的身份为人所知。满洲里站及周边所有地点拥有第18和第19军团的特工。然而，这并不妨碍第3号总部和第3号总部[原文重复]特工的工作。唯一的区别是，这些特工在开展工作时不与苏联直接联系，而是始终直接向哈尔滨报告。

在每个中国省会城市，都有一名专门的驻地人员负责覆盖全省的工作，他在所有县城都有特工。在没有县级特工的情况下，省级特工会有2或3名人员，按照预先计划的方案定期旅行并收集信息。省级驻地特工在省会城市以及县城行政机构收集的所有信息，都会通过专门信使定期（不少于每周一次）送往哈尔滨和海参崴。这些信使会带回新的指令、资金以及来自俄罗斯的私人信件。

All the secret agents of No 7 Headquarters have nothing in common
in their official work with the administrative organs of USSR. They do
not even have personal intercourse with the officials of the soviet
administrative institutions, for this could produce only a harm. The
only exception in this case affects certain places such as Dairen,
Chun Chun etc. where the agents of No 7 Headquarters worked as the
C.E.R. employees, prior to the conflict. This however was a rare excep-
tion. Apart from the inconvenience caused by amalgamating the activi-
ties of legal together with illegal work, there is another reason,
which prevents the agents of No 7 Headquarters from being employed on
the C.E.R. This reason is that the C.E.R. is monopolised by the G.P.U.
and consequently no secret agents of any of the other soviet branches
engaged in espionage work abroad, are allowed to be employees of the
C.E.R. No 7 Headquarters is very reluctant to give permission to its
agents to work on the C.E.R. as this involves the taking out soviet
citizenship. This is explained by the fact that soviet citizens are
being carefully watched by the police. It is only necessary to have a
soviet passport to be constantly dogged by some detective or other,
which, of course, spoils success. Therefore agents of No7 Headquarters
usually reside abroad either as employees or as subjects and citizens
of other countries and conduct their work exclusively by employing the
names of the foreign firms. etc. Some of the foreign commercial firms
never suspect that they are helping soviet espionage work. For in-
stance, none of the respectable American, British or German commercial
firms would have accepted soviet spies and afforded them the protection
of their respective flags had they known with whom they were dealing.
The insistence and often bare impertinence resorted to by the soviet
secret agents have no parallel. There is no person, no matter the po-
sition he may hold whom the Bolsheviks could not succeed in making use
of provided he represents some value to them.

An amusing case happened with one of the former Consuls in China.
This man possessed a large circle of Chinese connections, the result
of his former official position. These connections presented great value
to USSR. Attention was concentrated on him and it was ultimately dis-
covered that he had one failing namely a leaning towards one of the
branches of natural science. He was eventually exploited on this parti-
cular failing. Another case happened to a Chinese official who had
resided for a long time in Russia and was engaged in commerce. The Bol-
sheviks ruined him, so he returned to China with a deep hatred against the Bol-
sheviks. He entered the Government service and through the position he
held he was considered to be of considerable value to USSR. The Bolshe-
viks however knew that he would never consent to work for them, they
made him the proposal to work in the interests of Canton, that is to
say against the Northerners as war between the South and North was in
progress at that time. When the war ended and the unification of the
South and North was proclaimed, he continued to work for Feng Yu Hsiang.
Finally when it was no longer possible to deceive him as to his
real "masters" for whom he had worked, he was offered to work for the
Bolsheviks. He was absolutely powerless to refuse as he was totally in
the hands of the soviet agents by that time. One can be a determined enemy
of the Bolsheviks and yet work for them without being aware even from
the commencement from whom the instructions are issued.

第七总局的所有秘密特工在其公务工作中，与苏联的行政机关毫无共同之处。他们甚至不与苏维埃行政机构的官员进行私人交往，因为这样做只会带来危害。在此方面，唯一的例外涉及大连、长春（Chun Chun）（音译）等地，在冲突发生之前，第七总局的特工曾以中东铁路（C.E.R.）雇员的身份在那里工作。然而，这是一种罕见的例外。除了将合法活动与非法活动合并所带来的不便之外，还有另一个原因阻碍第七总局的特工受雇于中东铁路。这个原因是，中东铁路由国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）垄断，因此，任何其他从事海外间谍工作的苏维埃分支机构的秘密特工，都不被允许成为中东铁路的雇员。第七总局非常不情愿批准其特工在中东铁路工作，因为这涉及放弃苏联国籍。其原因在于，苏联公民受到警方的严密监视。只要持有苏联护照，就会不断被某位侦探或其他人员跟踪，这当然会破坏行动的成功。因此，第七总局的特工通常以其他国家的雇员或臣民及公民的身份居住在国外，并 exclusively 利用外国商号等名义开展工作。一些外国商业公司从未怀疑过它们正在协助苏联的间谍工作。例如，任何受人尊敬的美国、英国或德国商业公司，如果知道与之打交道的是谁，都不会接纳苏联间谍并给予其各自国旗的保护。苏联秘密特工所表现出的坚持乃至常常是赤裸裸的无礼，是无与伦比的。无论一个人身居何职，只要他对布尔什维克具有某种价值，他们就能成功地加以利用。

前驻华领事之一身上发生了一件有趣的事。此人因其以前的官方职位而拥有庞大的中国人脉关系网。这些关系对苏联具有巨大的价值。注意力集中在他身上，最终发现他有一个弱点，即倾向于自然科学的某一个分支。他最终因这一特定弱点而被利用。另一件事发生在一名长期居住在俄罗斯并从事实业的中国官员身上。布尔什维克毁了他，所以他怀着对布尔什维克的深切仇恨回到中国。他进入政府服务部门，凭借其所担任的职位，被认为对苏联具有相当大的价值。然而，布尔什维克知道他绝不会同意为他们工作，于是向他提议为广州的利益工作，也就是说，反对北方人，因为当时南北战争正在进行。当战争结束且南北统一宣告成立后，他继续为冯玉祥工作。最后，当再也无法就他为之效力的真正“主子”欺骗他时，便要求他为布尔什维克工作。他绝对无力拒绝，因为那时他已完全掌握在苏联特工手中。一个人可以是布尔什维克的坚定敌人，却在甚至从一开始就不知道指令来自何人的情况下为他们工作。
